meaningMnemonic: The moon has a lot of power that is power it gets from the power of every armpit of every human on earth! Why does your armpit smell? meaningMnemonic: When a flower looks like a mouth with horns that reach up to heaven , you know it's in blossom . It's all opened up like a mouth, and the pistil and stamen are like horns reaching up to heaven for its sunlight and rain. Hints Imagine studying this little blossom. Now imagine their tougher cousins, blossoms so tough you'd need a saw to cut them down. If you can picture the latter, you should remember the さ reading.

meaningMnemonic: Your servant uses a stool to break open shellfish . This is really clever , because shucking shellfish is a lot of work. It's also a wise move, because it'll save him time that he can spend on all his other servant chores. readingMnemonic: "Yes, more clever than you!" he yells, tearing off his servant's disguise. "It is I, Ken ( けん ) the samurai. I won't let you eat these shellfish. I'm taking them back to the sea, where they belong!" Hints Picture Ken standing there with his sword and crab-shell armor. Pretty clever of him to disguise himself as your servant for so many years just to save a few mollusks. It might have been wiser not to shuck so many of them first, though…

meaningMnemonic: You use a cleat to climb a tree and your hair gets the same coloring as the foliage because your hair is like a chameleon. Hints Imagine digging your cleats into the bark of the tree until you get high enough for your hair to start coloring itself tree colors. It might be a lot of work, but it's worth it.
readingMnemonic: This cool coloring can only happen because you turned yourself into a cy borg ( さい ). Your hair and scalp are now made of high tech parts, not human ones. Hints You couldn't take the pain of losing your cyborg, so you've become one. Your robo-hair can change its coloring, but soon you'll be even more cyborg-y than before!

meaningMnemonic: In this building there's a small sun that's small . They keep this small, small sun inside of a crevice . Hints You wouldn't want to keep a sun out in the open, even if it's small (and small). You'd put it inside something, like a crevice. Imagine walking into the building and seeing the small sun right inside, in a crevice.
readingMnemonic: They keep the sun in the crevice because this is a place where people ski ( すき ). Hints If the sun were out in the open, it'd melt all the snow, making it hard to ski here. So they hide the sun away in a crevice so people can ski.

meaningMnemonic: Your dirt needs a clown in it if you want to cultivate good crops. Hints Imagine burying a dead clown in the dirt and then planting some seeds on top. It's worth it, you think, if it helps cultivate your crops.
readingMnemonic: Before you can start this whole cultivation process however, you have to say bye ( ばい ) to the clown. Say bye to him, then bash his head in, and drop him in the dirt. Hints Saying bye is polite. Never forget to say bye, even in the middle of a cold-blooded clown murder.

meaningMnemonic: Your foot , as your mama says, was given the task to dance . Shake those two foots your mama gave you and dance dance dance! Hints Picture your mama asking you to dance. The two of you pick up and kick your feet to dance, spinning 'round and 'round.
readingMnemonic: You both dance so much that you develop an odo r ( おど ). Not just any odor, an odor particular to stinky dancing feet. Hints Lean down and take a big whiff of your dancing feet. The odor is... HORRIBLE! AHGH!

meaningMnemonic: This gate makes the sound of darkness . The gate looks like darkness, but it’s even more creepy that it sounds like darkness too. Hints Imagine this gate making an ominous sound. The sound of darkness. Look deep into the darkness of the gate as you hear the sound it makes. Ouummmmm…
readingMnemonic: You decide to taste the darkness and discover that it is so yummy ( やみ )! Who knew that darkness was so yummy? Mmm… this darkness tastes so yummy! Hints Take the darkness in your hands. It’s like really dark cotton candy. Imagine eating it and how yummy it is. Keep hearing the sound it’s making as you eat. Yummy!

meaningMnemonic: You have a surplus of ladle s laid out diagonally in front of you. Why are they diagonal? And why do you have so many ladles? Why the surplus? Hang on, we'll get there. Hints Look at all these ladles lying diagonally in front of you. Pick them up. Feel the wood grain. Wonder why you have so many.
readingMnemonic: In front of this diagonal pattern is a sha man ( しゃ ) who is currently staring at you. You slowly reach down and turn one of the ladles around, diagonally, and look back up. The shaman's eyes are wide, and now they're scribbling on in a notebook. Hints Uh oh, is this one of those weird tests where they find out if you're the chosen one or some old scholar reincarnated? Who knew laying ladles at diagonal angles could reveal this kinda stuff?!

meaningMnemonic: Melt down this gold book and recast it as a flower pot . A solid gold book is too heavy to hold and too shiny to read, but a solid gold flower pot would make a fancy new addition to your garden. Hints Imagine melting down your gold book. You're excited to have your new flower pot, but you're a little sad because this book was actually pretty interesting. Make a mental note to buy it in paperback later.
readingMnemonic: The gold flower pot has a hatch ( はち ) attached to it, which used to be the book's back cover. That's fine, you use the hatch as a lid for the flower pot! Hints Okay, so this may not be the best flower pot. You usually don't need a hatch or this much gold coating. But that's how they used to do it in the old days, so that's good enough for you!

meaningMnemonic: Rain falls off a tree and lands in your eye where it turns to frost . It turns to frost because it’s super cold outside and your body is freezing. The rain in your eye is wet, and then very cold as it becomes frost.
readingMnemonic: This whole description is pretty emo. You came up with this whole emo frost idea because you are a shemo ( しも ). An emo who goes by she pronouns. Hints Picture yourself walking proudly, casting your frost gaze at all who you pass. "Wow look at that frosty, cool shemo. She's sooooo cool!" you hear them whisper. (Haha cool, get it? Because you're frosty and also a little sad, which is totally in when you're a teen.)

meaningMnemonic: You need to feed this grain to a flower wearing turkey on a stool so you start the harvest . Grains don't pick themselves, you have to harvest them. meaningMnemonic: This canopy of tree s isn't actually a canopy of trees at all. When you look closely, you see these trees are actually giant stalks of hemp . Hints Wow, these hemp plants are so big that they look like trees. But, despite their size they're still just hemp.
readingMnemonic: Who planted all this hemp ? Your ma ma ( ま ) did. Hints Your mama knew that you were going to like hemp in the future, so she planted these hemp plants for you. What a great mama.

meaningMnemonic: Take your towel and make it long . It has to be longer than that! For this will be your notebook , which you will write all your notes in. Hints You are making the towel really long, because it's white and it might be good for writing in. It's going to become your notebook.

meaningMnemonic: The light shines on your forehead in your car with a great radiance . The car you are in is a convertible, so the light shines right onto your big bald forehead. Hints Imagine this radiance emanating from your shiny dome. The radiance is blinding!

Your car runs on reflected solar energy, and the radiance coming from your forehead is the most powerful source of radiant sunlight ever imagined. Your forehead is a perfect key for this car. Hints Point your shiny forehead, filled with radiance, at your car. Hear the engine start and jump to life as you power it with the reflected sunlight from your forehead.

meaningMnemonic: When your soul has an idea it's just a recollection of something you already know. Hmm, maybe you should move to Oklahoma and live the simple life again. Hints Imagine recollecting a past life in Oklahoma. Life was simple and nice. You should consider taking this as a sign to move there again!

meaningMnemonic: If you try to put your soul into every thing, you'll regret it. It's not so much that putting your soul into things is bad, but every single thing? You'll burn out immediately. Hints Imagine if you went full force into everything you've ever even thought of doing. Imagine how burnt out your soul would be. Imagine all the regret you'd have that you didn't just stick to one thing and do it well.
readingMnemonic: The regret is too strong for you to ignore, so you decide to drop everything but kay aking ( かい ). If there's one thing you refuse to regret, it's your bright orange kayak and all the friends you made at kayaking club. Hints Throw everything you regret away. Only kayak from now on.

meaningMnemonic: You take a rake in for a measurement but it is resistant . The rake doesn’t want to have its measurements taken. Hints Try and move this rake over to the measurement table. It is resistant so you have a hard time moving it. Imagine the rake struggling and resisting endlessly.
readingMnemonic: Because the rake is persistently resistant , you eventually tie it to the table with your neck tie ( たい ). The tie won’t hold for long, so you need to take each measurement quickly. Hints See yourself tying the tie around the rake and attaching it to the measurement table. The rake is still jostling around, but the tie keeps it from moving about too terribly much.

meaningMnemonic: On a cliff , the pope is holding a shield . The pope is near the edge of the cliff and is using the shield to fend off demons. The demons want to shove the pope off the cliff, but the pope is using his holy shield of popery to fend them off. Hints Imagine the shield glowing brightly as hymns play in the background. The demons try to get close to the pope to shove him off the cliff but the holy shield is too bright and popey.
readingMnemonic: The light of the pope's shield begins to fade. The shield's holy power is waning! Just as the demons are about to push him off the cliff, the sun begins to rise. That's right! Hints This pope would have been in a lot of trouble if June's summer sun hadn't risen at just the right moment. His shield would have become useless and he might have been shoved off the cliff if it was a less sunny month.

meaningMnemonic: There is an insect on the roof in a spoon . It's there for the eating, and it's how you plan to attract a snake to your roof. readingMnemonic: Why don't you just bring a snake up to the roof yourself? Because snakes are heavy ( へび ). Hints Especially big snakes. They're really, really hebi.

meaningMnemonic: If the king gives you a knife you become part of his squad . Every king has a knife squad or two protecting him and making sure his subjects keep in line. Hints Imagine if you were given a knife and allowed into the king's squad. Would you let the power corrupt you?

readingMnemonic: After you finish the table, you still feel like you might starve so you decide to eat every key ( き ) off your key ring. One by one, you eat each and every key so you don’t starve. readingMnemonic: You move at such swift speeds now, your jean s ( じん ) are ripped right off your body. Hints Fortunately, the lack of jeans make you even more swift and aerodynamic. You also feel a swift and pleasant breeze on all your downstairs bits now…

meaningMnemonic: What do you call the very tip of a cliff 's edge ? The brink . You can also simply call this the edge of a cliff . It's useful to know that 崖っ縁 means brink, though, because it's often used metaphorically to say that something is on the brink of something, whether it be catastrophe, death, or some other perilous situation. meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means amass and the verb vocab version is to store up — as in gradually gathering and keeping something so it's there when you need it. This often relates to storing up food or supplies. In the same vein, it can mean to amass a fortune for later use, or to build up things like stamina and knowledge to slowly prepare yourself for something. You can even say ヒゲを蓄える (to build up or grow facial hair). Readiness comes in many forms, you know?
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You need to store up things, so you take one ( たくわ ) and put it aside, then take one more and put it aside again. Repeat this to amass all kinds of things over time. It's the best way to build up a nice little stash.
